examples: Check which folder a pane is in before you paste a command.
how_to: Read the session's folder, what is running and the pane size at a glance.
For an agent session it also carries the model and usage meters.
The context meter is a colored gauge: green, blue, yellow, orange, then red as the conversation fills, with the percent in the same color.

The model leads on the left, then the three limits (ctx, 5h, 7d) as one group; the timers segment sits on the right, drawn only when it has something to say; the agents and shells segments are off by default and appear there only once you turn them on in settings. On a narrow cell the lowest priority pieces give way first (the 7d reset, the context fraction, the effort, then the 5h reset and the bars); the percentages and the work segments always stay. The agents and shells numbers are exactly the lengths of the control center's AGENTS (running) and SHELLS lists.

Click the bar to grow it into the session control center, full width and never resizing the session: every figure as a labeled band across the top (context/model/tokens, the two windows, cost/account), with timers, agents and shells as three equal columns underneath, each with its own count and stop-all. On a phone the band becomes tiles and the three lists become an accordion, one section open at a time.

Which items the collapsed bar shows (model, effort, context, either rate-limit window, agents, shells, timers) can be turned on or off individually (agents and shells start off, the rest start on); the grown view always shows everything regardless.

Three layouts are built for the collapsed bar and three for the grown one, picked independently in settings (next to the status bar items list): collapsed A (meters first, default), B (a text status line grouped into session/account scopes) or C (attention-first, one meter for whichever limit is closest to its end); open A (a summary band plus three columns, default), B (a tabs rail: usage/timers/agents/shells) or C (one merged list grouped by owner, with filter chips).
